hookAlternatives.text: Less than a second after liftoff, Challenger was already leaking.
hookAlternatives.for: Opens on the cause, not the outcome; raises the question the film answers (how could it fly 73 s with a leak?). Matches an authentic NASA photo of the smoke at frame 0. Not the title read aloud.
hookAlternatives.against: Needs the viewer to accept 'leaking' before the mechanism is shown; the photo's smoke is small on a phone, so it needs a marker.

hookAlternatives.text: Seventy-three seconds after launch, Challenger broke apart.
hookAlternatives.against: It is the published title and the published opening (Version A) - repeats what the viewer already read; leads with the loss of the crew, which pulls the opening toward the breakup footage the original looped.

hookAlternatives.text: The night before launch, engineers said: not below fifty-three degrees. Challenger launched at thirty-six.
hookAlternatives.against: Two numbers in the first 3 s; risks implying every decision maker heard the warning (the Commission found Levels I and II did not); spends the payoff before the mechanism is understood.

chosenHookReason: H1 is the only opening that is (a) new to a viewer who read the title, (b) answerable by the film's own causal chain, (c) supported by an authentic NASA photograph that can fill the first frame, and (d) not built on the moment of the crew's death. H3's decision material is kept for the payoff, where the mechanism has been explained and the Commission's nuance (the objection never reached top officials) fits.
